correctness.rationale: Conditioned on any k quota-exact elected candidate columns, at most n-q voters remain unrepresented. For an unselected independent column the unrepresented approval count is binomial with mean at most (n-q)p; its gap below q is >=n/(2k^2) eventually. Hoeffding gives exp(-n/(2k^4)); a polynomial union bound works simultaneously for all eligible committees. The independent quota-count is exactly Binomial(m,a), with sqrt(n)a tending to the stated Gaussian density. The Poisson committee-count law and expectation follow, plus Chernoff off criticality. Verification code exhaustively compares JR definitions in small cases; it is not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Chingoma et al. (2026) introduced DR and its worst-case computational status, but the inspected DR section, appendix, and experiments do not give random-approval critical supply or the Poisson committee-count law. Han et al. (2025) study AJR with constant candidate supply and no exact-support constraint; Elkind et al. prove asymptotically all fixed-candidate-size committees are JR (Theorem 3.1/Proposition 1) in the independent model, but not growing-candidate exact-support DR counts. The earlier general JR results do not imply the binomial rare-support threshold or the joint limit for DR committees. A deterministic quota-support shortcut under additional structural hypotheses does not imply this random scaling, simultaneous JR event, or limit theorem.

value.rationale: This is the first natural asymptotic feasibility question for an explicitly exact-support voting axiom: a square-root candidate-supply threshold with full critical Poisson limiting distribution, and a simultaneous high-probability structural reduction from JR plus exact support to exact support alone. It explains a gap between worst-case DR hardness/insatisfiability and large random electorates, and gives a quantitative count of available committees; not a cosmetic statistic or predetermined tiny finite slice.
